Google folds the variants users type (ه for ة, ا for أ/إ/آ, ي for ى), as the autocomplete data shows ('علامه مائيه' and 'علامة مائية' complete to each other).

formats.htmlLang: <html lang="ar" dir="rtl"> on every /ar page. Do not set dir from client JavaScript only: crawlers and the first paint must already be RTL.
formats.ogLocale: ar_AR (Facebook/Open Graph's Arabic locale). No og:locale:alternate regional variants.

digits.rule: Use Western digits (0–9) everywhere, in static HTML and in runtime formatting. Format with Intl and the locale 'ar-u-nu-latn-ca-gregory', never bare 'ar-SA' / 'ar-EG' / 'ar-IQ'.
why: Searchers type Western digits: '4k', '1080', 'mp4', 'mp3', '2024', '2026' in every completion collected.
Pin IDs, resolutions (720p, 1080p, 1200 × 1200), file sizes and filenames are technical tokens that must match what the user sees in URLs and file managers.

Morocco and the UAE use Western digits by default (ICU 78 / CLDR 48: Intl.NumberFormat('ar-MA') → '1.234,5', 'ar-AE' → '1,234.5'). Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Iraq default to Arabic-Indic ('ar-SA' → '١٬٢٣٤٫٥'), but those readers read Western digits on the web without friction. Mixing the two systems on one page looks broken.
In the same ICU build, bare 'ar' already returns Western digits ('1,234.5'), but older browsers and Safari can return Arabic-Indic for bare 'ar'. Pass '-u-nu-latn' explicitly.
digits.avoid: Arabic-Indic digits (٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩) and Persian digits (۰۱۲۳). Do not mix them with Western digits anywhere on the page.

decimal.rule: Avoid decimals in static copy (write '12 MB', '720p', '1200 بكسل'). When the UI must show one, format with Intl.NumberFormat('ar-u-nu-latn') → '12.4'.
decimal.why: Morocco uses a decimal comma ('12,4'); the Gulf, Egypt and Iraq use a point (or the Arabic decimal separator '٫' with Arabic-Indic digits). One Arabic page serves both, so keep decimals out of static text.

formats.thousands: Do not group 4-digit numbers (1080, 1200, 2026). Never group pin IDs or serials. In runtime counts above 9999, Intl 'ar-u-nu-latn' gives '12,345'.
formats.percent: 50% (Western digits; Intl 'ar-u-nu-latn' emits LRM marks around % so it stays in place in RTL). Avoid percentages in marketing copy anyway (no fabricated stats).
formats.dimensions: 1200 × 1200 بكسل. Put the numeric part inside <bdi dir="ltr"> so the × and digits keep their order inside an RTL sentence.
formats.resolution: 720p, 1080p, 4K in Latin, inside <bdi>. Arabic sentence form: 'بدقة 1080p'.
formats.fileSize: 12 MB / 800 KB (Latin unit abbreviations; Intl unit formatting in Arabic prints 'م.ب', which most people do not recognise).

date.rule: Gregorian calendar, Western digits, Arabic month names in the Egyptian/Gulf form: '14 أكتوبر 2026'. Format with new Intl.DateTimeFormat('ar-u-nu-latn-ca-gregory', {dateStyle: 'long'}).
date.why: Iraq and the Levant use the Syriac month names ('تشرين الأول'), the Maghreb sometimes uses French-derived names ('أكتوبر' is still understood everywhere). 'أكتوبر' reads correctly in all five markets. Some browser and ICU versions default 'ar-SA' to the Umm al-Qura Hijri calendar, so pass 'ca-gregory' explicitly. For machine-readable dates keep ISO 8601 in <time datetime> and JSON-LD.

formats.time: Avoid clock times in content. If needed: 24-hour '14:30' in Western digits.
formats.readTime: '5 دقائق للقراءة'. Arabic counted nouns change with the number: 1 'دقيقة واحدة', 2 'دقيقتان', 3–10 'دقائق', 11 and up 'دقيقة'. Use Intl.PluralRules('ar') (see plurals).
formats.wordCount: '1,240 كلمة' / '850 كلمة' (11 and up takes the singular 'كلمة'; 3–10 take 'كلمات').

plurals.rule: Arabic has six plural categories (zero, one, two, few = 3–10, many = 11–99, other = 100+ and 0 in some styles). Intl.PluralRules('ar').select(n) returns them (verified: 0 zero, 1 one, 2 two, 3 few, 11 many, 100 other). Every string with a count needs all six forms or must avoid the counted noun.
plurals.fallback: Where a component cannot take plural forms, use a label plus number ('المنشورات: 12'), which is correct for any count.

formats.quotes: Use «…» for quoted Pinterest labels in running text (for example «نسخ الرابط»). Inside UI buttons, no quotes.
formats.punctuation: Arabic comma '،' (U+060C), semicolon '؛' (U+061B) and question mark '؟' (U+061F) in Arabic sentences. FAQ questions end with '؟'. Keep '.' and ':' as they are. Do not put the Arabic comma inside Latin tokens (MP4، ZIP is fine; 1080p, 720p stays Latin when listed alone).
formats.capitalisation: Not applicable to Arabic. Latin tokens keep their casing: PintDownload, Pinterest, MP4, GIF, ZIP, iPhone, Safari, Chrome. Do not apply text-transform: uppercase to mixed Arabic/Latin labels (it would uppercase 'pin.it' and filenames).
formats.currency: Not needed (free). Keep JSON-LD offers price '0' and priceCurrency 'USD' as the English pages do; it is not shown.
formats.abbreviations: Avoid Arabic abbreviations in UI (no 'م.ب', no 'ص/م'). 'إلخ' is fine in prose.
formats.diacritics: No full vowelling. Add a diacritic only where it changes meaning or reading: shadda in imperatives ('حمّل', 'حوّل', 'جرّب'), tanween on adverbs ('مجانًا', 'رابطًا'). Every diacritic counts as a character in the title/description length checks, which use Python len() on code points.
formats.tatweel: Never use tatweel/kashida (ـ) to stretch words or justify text.

notes.hreflangDecision: Use hreflang='ar' and <html lang='ar' dir='rtl'>. No regional variants. Reasons: (1) The five markets search almost identically: in batch 1, 404 of 484 market/seed pairs returned the same suggestion set as Saudi Arabia (mean Jaccard 0.92), and the differences are long-tail reorderings. (2) The pages are written in Modern Standard Arabic, which every market reads. (3) A regional tag such as ar-SA or ar-EG would leave the other markets, and the many other Arabic-speaking countries (Jordan, Kuwait, Algeria and others), on x-default English. (4) Google's hreflang documentation accepts an ISO 639-1 language code alone, and region subtags must be ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, so 'ar-001' and similar macro-region codes are not supported. (5) Competitors that bother with hreflang declare plain 'ar' (KlickPin, PinDown, PinterestDownloader.io). Wire it in pairs: each English page lists hreflang='en' (itself) + hreflang='ar' (/ar/...) + x-default (English); each Arabic page lists the same set. Skipped pages get no 'ar' alternate. og:locale = ar_AR.
notes.urlStructure: /ar for the home page (no trailing slash, as normalizeCanonical requires for non-root paths) and /ar/<english-slug> for the rest. Keep the English slugs and do not transliterate. Reasons: (1) Arabic searchers never type Latin transliterations of Arabic words ('tahmil-fidyo' carries no query match), so a transliterated slug would be noise. (2) Arabic-script slugs would match queries, but they become long percent-encoded strings (/ar/%D8%AA%D8%AD%D9%85%D9%8A%D9%84-…) when copied into WhatsApp, the region's main sharing channel. They also mix directions inside the LTR address bar and need encoding care in canonical URLs, the sitemap, IndexNow and hostRedirectUrl (the task's ASCII-only rule rules them out anyway). (3) The English slugs contain English queries that Arabic-locale users really type: 'pinterest video downloader', 'pinterest to mp4', 'pinterest board downloader', 'pinterest gif downloader' all complete with hl=ar. (4) Identical slugs make hreflang pairing and the language switcher trivial. (5) The Arabic tool competitors (KlickPin, PinDown, pinterestvideo.com) also keep English slugs under /ar/. URL words are a minor signal; titles, H1s and body copy carry the Arabic keywords. Add the /ar routes to SITEMAP_ROUTES with xhtml:link alternates.
notes.msaAndDialects: Write Modern Standard Arabic in a plain, friendly register: second person masculine singular imperatives ('الصق', 'حمّل', 'احفظ'), as Arabic UIs conventionally do. Avoid dialect in copy. Dialect queries ('ازاي احمل' EG, 'كيفاش نحمل' MA, 'شلون احمل' IQ, 'كيف اقدر احفظ' Gulf) all exist and complete with 'بدون علامه مائيه'. Google maps them to the same intent, so MSA pages can rank for them without writing dialect. Device and app words: 'الجوال' (Gulf) with 'الموبايل' once; 'الكمبيوتر' over 'الحاسوب'; 'الاستديو' and 'المعرض' both.
notes.marketDifferences: Small: EG adds 'تحميل بنترست apk', 'تحميل بنترست لايت', 'تنزيل بنترست إصدار قديم' (app installs) and 'للمعرض' instead of 'إلى الاستديو'. AE uses 'جوده عاليه' where others say 'بدقة عالية'. IQ adds 'للحاسوب', 'بدون علامه تيك توك', Syriac month names, and English tool brands (pingrab, pinload). MA completes more English ('pinterest downloader bot'). None justifies a regional page.
intentTraps: 'تحميل بنترست' / 'تنزيل بنترست' / 'بنترست تحميل' (no 'من') mostly mean installing the Pinterest app (apk، لايت، للكمبيوتر، من جوجل/قوقل، إصدار قديم، للاندرويد، للايفون، ويندوز). Target 'تحميل من بنترست' and say early that PintDownload is a website, not the app.
'تحميل بنترست على اللابتوب / الكمبيوتر / الحاسوب / الماك بوك' = install the app; 'تحميل الفيديو من بنترست للكمبيوتر' = our intent.
'بنترست بدون حساب' is mostly browsing Pinterest without signing up (صور بنات، خلفيات، بحث google). Only 'تحميل … بدون حساب' is ours.
'صور بنترست', 'صور بروفايل', 'pfp بنترست' = looking for images or profile-picture ideas, not a downloader.
'لوحة بنترست' = vision boards and drawings (لوحة الاهداف، لوحة تخرج، رسم).
'قصص بنترست' = children's stories; 'ستوري بنترست' = Instagram story ideas.

honestyRisks: Watermark: say 'لا نضيف أي علامة مائية' (we add none), not 'نزيل العلامة المائية' (we remove watermarks). Logos burned into a video by its uploader stay. Pinterest's own in-app video download is a creator opt-in that stamps the creator's name and username. Downloading a video the creator chose not to make downloadable is a rights question: keep the 'credit the creator / personal use' line next to the watermark claim.

Image size: the extractor serves the public 1200x size because /originals/ is often blocked (src/lib/pin-media.ts). Never write 'الحجم الأصلي', 'بدون ضغط', or '4K' for images. The English image page says 'Save HD Original Photos'; flag it.

Video quality: 720p/1080p/540p MP4 only (src/lib/extract/media.ts quality labels). The English 4K page claims '4K ultra quality' and 'original uncompressed MP4'. The Arabic HD page must not, and the English page should be corrected.

MP3: the 'MP3' download is the MP4 video URL saved with a .mp3 filename (DownloaderForm.tsx: entries.push({ url: vUrl, filename: `${safeTitle}_audio.mp3` }); saveProxyDownload(videoUrl, mp3Name)). Do not localise 'Download MP3 Sound' or 'استخراج الصوت' into Arabic until real audio extraction exists. This also affects the English audio page.
Profile picture: do not print 'HD' or 'الحجم الكامل'; say 'بأكبر حجم متاح'.

No user counts, ratings, 'أفضل موقع', 'الأسرع', or performance claims (SavePin's 'أداء وإنجازات' section is the pattern to avoid). No aggregateRating in JSON-LD (the invariant test already enforces this).
Not affiliated: 'PintDownload موقع مستقل وغير تابع لشركة Pinterest' in the footer and on the home page, in Arabic, not only in English.

rtl.documentDirection: Set <html lang="ar" dir="rtl"> server-side in BaseLayout for /ar routes. The current LanguageSelector sets the direction client-side over English HTML; that must not be how /ar pages get RTL.
rtl.logicalProperties: Convert physical CSS to logical properties before launching /ar: the audit found ~53 'text-left', 4 'border-l-2', 2 'border-r-2', 1 'text-right' in components, and ~46 physical left/right declarations in src/styles (blog.css 17, results.css 20, ticket.css 9). Tailwind 3.4 already ships 'text-start', 'ms-*/me-*', 'ps-*/pe-*', 'start-*/end-*', 'border-s/e' and the 'rtl:' variant.

ticketGeometry.header: Label 'تذكرة دخول · رابط عام' on the start side (right), serial 'رقم …' on the end side (left).
ticketGeometry.stubTear: The stub hinges from its top-left corner today (transform-origin: 0% 0%; translate(6px, 18px) rotate(-3.5deg)). In RTL hinge from the top-right: transform-origin: 100% 0%; translate(-6px, 18px) rotate(3.5deg). Reduced motion stays a fade.
ticketGeometry.receipts: The wide receipt split (7fr / 5fr) mirrors with the grid automatically if columns use logical order; the dashed vertical perforation moves with it. The number tag ('01/05') sits top-right; the kind stamp sits bottom-left.

typography.displayFace: Big Shoulders Display has no Arabic glyphs, and the repo only ships its Latin subset (public/fonts/big-shoulders-display-latin-800/900). Pair it with a heavy Arabic display face for H1s, H2s, labels, stamps and the stub. Candidates (all SIL OFL on Google Fonts, self-hostable, with 800/900 weights): 'Alexandria' (geometric, drawn from Egyptian street signage, which fits the printed-ticket world), 'Noto Kufi Arabic' (Kufi, 100–900), 'Cairo' (200–1000). Subset to Arabic plus the Latin the page needs, preload only on /ar routes, and keep Big Shoulders for Latin tokens (MP4, 1080p, pin IDs) through the font-family stack.
typography.bodyFace: The system sans stack covers Arabic: SF Arabic on iOS/macOS, Noto Sans Arabic on Android, Segoe UI on Windows. No webfont is needed for reading text.
typography.noUppercaseNoTracking: Under :lang(ar), set text-transform: none and letter-spacing: 0 on t-label, t-display, serial, stub and stamps. Arabic has no case, and tracking pulls the joined letters apart.
typography.lineHeight: Arabic display text needs line-height around 1.2–1.3. The current 0.88–0.9 clips the dots and the tall letters (ك ل ط) and makes stacked lines collide.
typography.size: Arabic reads smaller than Latin at the same font-size. Keep inputs at ≥16px and consider 1.125rem for body copy on /ar.
typography.italics: Never italicise Arabic (browsers fake a slant). Use bold or colour for emphasis.
typography.underline: Increase text-underline-offset on Arabic links so the line clears the dots below letters (ب ي ج).

bidi.mixedTokens: Wrap Latin and numeric runs that touch punctuation or other numbers in <bdi> (or <span dir="ltr">): 'MP4 (1080p)', 'pin.it/AbC123', filenames, pin IDs, '1200 × 1200'. Otherwise parentheses and punctuation jump to the wrong side.
bidi.urls: Every URL shown to the reader (pin.it examples, https://www.pinterest.com/username/board/) goes inside <code dir="ltr"> or <bdi>. The site's own /ar/... paths are ASCII and LTR; that is intentional (see notes.urlStructure).
bidi.pasteInput: The URL input must type LTR (dir="ltr", inputmode="url") while its Arabic placeholder reads RTL. Use: input:placeholder-shown { direction: rtl; text-align: right } and input:not(:placeholder-shown) { direction: ltr; text-align: left }. Keep the paste/clear buttons on the logical end.
bidi.titleTag: Arabic titles end with ' | PintDownload'. The browser renders the Latin brand at the visual left of an RTL title; that is correct and needs no RLM marks.
bidi.jsonLd: JSON-LD text fields take plain Arabic strings; do not insert bidi control characters into structured data.

icons.mirror: Directional arrows and chevrons (next/back, breadcrumb separators, 'read more' arrows, the dashed lead arrows in the how-to illustrations).
icons.doNotMirror: Download (down arrow), play, check, clock, the logo, the Pinterest-like pin mark, media controls and progress spinners, plus anything that depicts a real object.

rtl.illustrations: public/images/step1–3.webp show English labels and a left-to-right flow. Arabic pages need Arabic versions with mirrored flow, or neutral versions with Arabic alt text. Do not ship English screenshots on Arabic pages.
rtl.tablesAndScrollers: Sticky first column sits on the right (inset-inline-start: 0). Horizontal scrollers start at the right edge in RTL; check that scroll shadows and 'scroll for more' hints mirror.
rtl.breadcrumbs: Crumbs run right to left (الرئيسية first, on the right). Use a chevron icon that mirrors under dir=rtl, not a hard-coded '›' glyph.

notes.searchCentral: Google hreflang rules applied: language codes in ISO 639-1; optional region in ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; return links required on both sides; x-default for the English fallback; one canonical per language version, self-referencing (not pointing at English, which is PinterestDownloader.io's mistake). Google treats URL words as a very light signal and reads the page language from visible content, so the Arabic copy, not the slug, decides language matching.
